caption: Four store accounts took six years to build. How long did yours take?

slides.title:
How I'm clearing
R38 000 of store
debt on R15 300 p/m
Living in Cradock
slides.body:
Female, 37
Single, one son (9)
Job: Sales consultant, clothing store
Net salary: R15 300 p/m
Debt: R38 000 across four store accounts

slides.title: Rent
slides.body: A two bedroom because he needs his own room for homework. I will not trade that.

slides.title: Store account payments
slides.body: Three clothing accounts and one furniture account. I opened them one at a time, over six years.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.body: I buy the cheaper brand now. He has not noticed. I have.

slides.title: Transport
slides.includes: Taxi to the shop, taxi back, a lift on Sundays
slides.body: Twelve taxi rides a week. I counted once, then stopped counting.

slides.title: Staff discount clothes
slides.includes: Two tops and a pair of school shoes, plus one pair for me
slides.body: I work at a clothing store and still buy clothes. I know what that sounds like.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: black tax, prepaid electricity, funeral policy, stokvel, airtime, school costs
slides.body: Six small amounts, R2 880. The stokvel is the only line here that gives money back to me in December.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R15 300. It is not a lot, but it is the first month I did not need to borrow from my cousin.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I put all four store accounts into Beyond Horizon's debt tracker and compared snowball with avalanche.

The interest cost was different between them.

No bank login needed.
